what_it_does: Fuzzing is a security-testing technique where a tool automatically feeds huge numbers of unusual or malformed inputs to a program and watches for crashes or misbehavior. For Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices, the software that handles network communication (the "protocol implementation") must be tested this way. The challenge is that IoT protocol software often behaves very differently depending on which configuration settings are active — certain bugs only appear under specific combinations of settings. Traditional fuzzers test with a fixed configuration, so they miss entire categories of bugs. CMFuzz solves this by first reverse-engineering a general model of how a protocol's configuration options relate to each other, then using that model to spread different configurations intelligently across many fuzzing processes running in parallel. This way the fuzzer explores configuration-dependent code paths that would otherwise never be reached.
